Mia Chen: quick timeout — seeing a tiny latency regression on batch=8 perf runs after the latest kv-cache change, can someone help collect a minimal nsys + torch.prof trace?
Samir Patel: I can grab one, can you paste the exact command and the env you used?
Mia Chen: thanks! run used: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6 python serve_bench.py --model rwdl/llama-mini --batch 8 --seq 512 --profile nsys`
Mia Chen: capture size was ~1.2GB which is annoying to share. ideally want a tiny repro (1-2 requests) and a flamegraph/KPIs.
Alex G.: for nsys, use the lightweight set: `nsys profile --output mini_trace --sample=cpu -t cuda,osrt,cudaProfilerApi --force python serve_bench.py --short-run`
Alex G.: then run torch.prof hook around forward to get op-level breakdown, e.g. insert `with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[...], record_shapes=True) as p: ...; p.export_chrome_trace('tprof.json')`
perf-bot: automated notice — trace uploads > 1GB will be archived. consider `--sample=kernel` or shorter duration.
Kevin L: if you want a minimal reproducer i can strip the workload to single-batch call. here's a tiny script you can drop in: ```python
# tiny_repro.py
import torch, time
from model import load_model
model = load_model('rwdl/llama-mini').cuda().eval()
x = torch.randint(0, 1000, (1,512)).cuda()
with torch.no_grad():
    for _ in range(2):
        t0 = time.time(); out = model(x); print('ms', (time.time()-t0)*1000)
```
Kevin L: run that under nsys for ~2 iterations and it should be <200MB trace.
Tara V: question — if we upload to the perf bucket, does the infra team auto-scrub hostnames and tokens? we should confirm before sharing.
Mia Chen: good point — i redacted keys but left hostnames. i can sanitize with `nsys export --sanitize` (?) not sure exact flag.
Samir Patel: nsys doesn't have a one-liner sanitize; we usually `nsys export` then run our scrubber script: `scripts/scrub_trace.py mini_trace.qdrep --strip-hostnames`
Alex G.: also strip /tmp paths from torch.prof chrome trace before sharing. trivial jq + sed.
Tara V: if you want, upload to `s3://redwood-perf/temp/mia-2924/` and tag with `needs-scrub`. infra will pick it up. ping me when done and i'll fast-track scrub.
Mia Chen: uploading now to s3, link: s3://redwood-perf/temp/mia-2924/mini_trace.qdrep (will mark needs-scrub).
perf-bot: upload registered: s3://redwood-perf/temp/mia-2924/mini_trace.qdrep (id: pf-2924681357).
Samir Patel: grabbing it now, will run the flamegraph flow and post a trimmed SVG here.
Kevin L: if samir is taking it, i can try to reproduce on A100 to check hw variance.
Mia Chen: that would be awesome. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Tara V: noted — i'll watch for the scrub job and then grant access to the SRE perf group.
Samir Patel: quick status — trimmed flamegraph looks like a few extra memcpy spikes right before KV warmup, pushing tail latency. sharing SVG in 10m.
Mia Chen: perfect, i'll file a small regression ticket with the flamegraph link and the sample script. thanks all.
Alex G.: also adding a queued task to try `torch.compile` toggles as an experiment.
Mia Chen: ack.
